_comment: watch-your-step rules. Data, not code: add a rule here plus a should_flag and a should_pass case in tests/cases.json. context = which parts of the command the pattern sees: bare (unquoted shell), squote, dquote, heredoc_quoted (<<'EOF' body, literal), heredoc_unquoted (<<EOF body, expanded), raw (the whole command). check = regex (default) or a named builtin check. shells = only for these login shells (empty = all). tools = tool names the rule applies to.

rules.message: a backtick inside a double-quoted string (or an unquoted <<EOF heredoc) is command substitution: the code span is replaced by the output of running it, and the command still exits 0.
rules.fix: single-quote the prose, use a quoted heredoc (<<'EOF'), or escape each backtick as \`

rules.message: a literal like "$40" or "$0" inside double quotes is a positional parameter: it expands (usually to nothing) and the text changes silently.
rules.fix: single-quote the text, or escape it as \$40
rules.incident: 2026-09-27, a waypoint bullet lost its dollar amount

rules.message: this path names a home directory that is not yours. Models rebuild a path from token pieces each time they write it, so the user name can come out mistyped; the tool then reports a missing FILE, never a wrong DIRECTORY.
rules.fix: write the path as ~/... (native file tools accept it) or $HOME/... in shell, never the expanded home directory
rules.incident: 2026-10-24, a free-lane session wrote two different misspellings of the user name in absolute paths

rules.message: this command truncates a file before it reads it (`cmd f > f`, or python open(p, "w") ... open(p).read()): the shell or python empties the file first, so the read sees nothing and the file is destroyed while the command reports success.
rules.fix: write to a temp file and move it over the original (preserving its mode), or edit in place with the Edit tool
rules.incident: file-rewrite trap, recorded in the shell one-liners memory

rules.message: in zsh an unquoted word starting with '=' (like ==== or ==) is EQUALS expansion: zsh looks it up as a command, fails with '=== not found', and aborts the REST of the command line.
rules.fix: quote it ('====') or use a different separator such as '----'
rules.incident: 2026-09-30, and again 2026-10-24: a probe's later stages never ran

rules.message: ${PIPESTATUS[0]} is a bash-ism; the Bash tool here runs zsh, where it is empty, so an exit-status check built on it always passes.
rules.fix: in zsh use $pipestatus[1] (lower case, 1-based), or run the pipeline under bash explicitly

rules.message: grep -F treats ^ as a literal character, so an anchored needle can never match and the search silently finds nothing.
rules.fix: drop -F and escape the needle, or drop the ^ anchor

rules.message: zsh does NOT word-split an unquoted $var, so `for f in $files` runs ONCE with the whole list as one argument.
rules.fix: use ${=files} or an array (files=(...); for f in $files), or read lines with ${(f)files}
rules.incident: 2026-10-16, free-agents release: a loop processed one 'file'

rules.message: this commit / rebase --continue would record conflict markers (<<<<<<< or >>>>>>> lines) as the resolution: staging a still-conflicted file marks it resolved, git succeeds, and every later reader of the file gets garbage.
rules.fix: resolve the markers in the file, re-stage it, and check with  git diff --cached --check  before continuing
rules.incident: 2026-10-14, a plugin manifest reached public main with conflict markers inside; every installer then saw the old version

rules.message: this worktree holds gitignored files (not caches) that `git worktree remove` deletes for good; 'clean and merged' hides them, because status --porcelain does not list ignored files.
rules.fix: list them with  git -C <worktree> status --porcelain --ignored , compare each with history or the main checkout, and copy anything unique OUTSIDE the repo first
rules.incident: 2026-10-19, a removed worktree held the only copy of a plan's progress ledger

rules.message: a bare glob that matches nothing ABORTS the whole zsh command line before anything runs: the only output is '(eval):N: no matches found', and earlier or simultaneous stages silently never execute.
rules.fix: quote the pattern when the TOOL should expand it (find . -name '*.log', grep --include), add the (N) glob qualifier, or setopt NULL_GLOB in the same command
rules.incident: 2026-10-20, a find A /tmp/la-* probe was killed by its glob and the empty output nearly read as 'no logs exist'

rules.message: git worktree add starts the new worktree from HEAD, not from the working tree: the source checkout's uncommitted files stay behind, and the new tree will not contain them.
rules.fix: commit a WIP checkpoint in the source checkout first, or copy the paths across deliberately after the add
rules.incident: 2026-10-25, playbook-rules plan: the coverage grep found no hook guarding worktree-dirty while the standard workflow assumes clean sources

rules.message: ps/pgrep output that includes full process arguments (aux/ax, -ef or -e -f, -ww, -o args/command/cmd, pgrep -a / -fl / --list-full) can carry API keys from a command line into the transcript.
rules.fix: ps -o pid,lstart,comm -p <pids>, or pgrep -x <name>: identify processes without widening the output to argv
rules.incident: 2026-10-25 handoff standing rule: never print process argv — a key handed to a child process on its command line lands in the output

rules.message: git stash without -u / --include-untracked / -a leaves untracked files in the working tree while the stash looks like it saved everything; a later clean or checkout can then destroy them.
rules.fix: git stash -u, or commit to a named WIP checkpoint branch instead — a branch is more visible than a stash
rules.incident: backup-before-editing-uncommitted-work: tracked ≠ recoverable, and untracked work is the part a plain stash silently omits

rules.message: zsh does not word-split an unquoted $var, so `cmd $files 2>/dev/null` passes the whole list as ONE argument (usually a nonexistent path); with stderr discarded the failure reads as a clean empty result.
rules.fix: use ${=files} or an array ($files[@]), or xargs; never trust an empty search that hides its own stderr without a planted positive control
rules.incident: 2026-10-25, observation 0046: 17 coverage greps printed nothing, including the planted positive control
